## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: when the command adopts an existing setting, it now prints the adoption message twice, because `plan` emits it as progress and `run` then renders the new `adopt` change as well. This review read `app/planner.py`, `app/cli.py`, and `tests/test_planner.py` in full and traced each change kind through `run`'s rendering loop. It did not run the tests. Audit records are correctly left out of command output, and `tests/test_planner.py:24` asserts that for the empty-input case.

## Changes
`plan` now records an `adopt` change for each setting that already exists and adds an `audit` change at the end with the number of incoming settings. The PR adds two tests for the audit record and a one-line `app/review.txt` file.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Stop emitting adoption messages twice from `run` — Calling `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` now sends `"Adopted theme"` to `emit` twice. `plan` emits it as progress at `app/planner.py:8`, and then `app/cli.py:6-9` emits the message of every change that is not an `audit`, which now includes the new `adopt` change. No test calls `run` with a setting that already exists: `test_adoption_progress` calls `plan` directly, so it still passes. — Every adopted setting appears twice in command output, which contradicts the PR body's statement that the command "continues to render actionable changes and omit audit records". — Fix: Either have `app/cli.py` skip `adopt` changes the same way it skips `audit`, or stop calling `emit` inside `plan` and let `run` handle all rendering. Then add a `run` test with an existing setting that asserts `messages == ["Adopted theme"]`.
